title: The Noise Floor of Agent Evaluation: Live Generation, Replay, and Rerun Budgets
content: Agent evaluations can compress stochastic generation, execution, and model-based judging into a single score,obscuring whether a measured difference reflects a change in the system or variability in the evaluation itself. Here,we introduce the determinism ladder, a measurement framework that compares fresh generation, temperature-zerogeneration, and content-addressed replay through executable verification, together with a frozen-candidate experimentthat distinguishes variability in judge verdicts from disagreement with executed outcomes. Across HumanEval+ andMBPP+ in two hosted model-and-verifier stacks, we found that replay nearly eliminated the observed within-taskvariation. In the primary stack, live variances of 0.0301 and 0.0142 fell to 0 and 0.0010 under replay, while a secondstack reproduced the same ordering. Temperature zero also reduced generation variance in both stacks, althoughthe remaining variation was stack-specific. On 200 frozen MBPP+ candidates, a stochastic judge introduced verdictvariance of 0.0073. Setting the judge temperature to zero removed the observed verdict variation, yet majority verdictsstill disagreed with executed outcomes on 23.5% of tasks, demonstrating that repeatability and reference agreementare distinct properties of an evaluation. For an illustrative fixed-task difference of 0.02, the measured variancescorresponded to point budgets of 3–8 runs per arm under live evaluation and one under valid replay, subject to the statedplanning assumptions. Together, these results show that evaluation variability can be measured under stage-specificcontrols rather than absorbed into a single score, providing a basis for matching replication and evaluation design tothe claim an agent benchmark is intended to support.
